title: Constitutional convention
officialText: Shall a convention of elected delegates be convened in 2027 to draft a general revision of the State Constitution for presentation to the state’s voters for their approval or rejection?
plainEnglish: This asks whether Michigan should hold a constitutional convention in 2027.

If voters say yes, Michigan would elect delegates to write a full revision of the state constitution. That draft would then be put on a later statewide ballot, and voters would decide whether to accept or reject it.
A yes vote calls the convention. A no vote means the convention is not held, and the current constitution stays in place unless it is changed some other way.
summary: This asks whether Michigan should call a convention in 2027 to draft a revised state constitution. Voters would later accept or reject that draft. It is a yes-or-no question. Ballotpedia lists it as Proposal 1, a constitutional-convention question automatically referred to the ballot.

title: Campaign finance
officialText: A Proposed Initiated Law to Prohibit Campaign Contributions for Certain Regulated Utilites and Government Contractors and Apply Campaign Finance Laws and Regulations to Additional Types of Political Communications The proposal would: • Prohibit regulated electric and gas utilities, contractors with over $250,000 annually in government contracts, and people and organizations with substantial connections to these utilities/contractors from making direct or indirect campaign contributions to those who run for or hold offices that impact them. • Expand laws regulating spending on political communications, including those requiring disclosing donor information, to apply to communications clearly identifying candidates or ballot questions, even if they do not expressly advocate voting for/against them. • Expressly apply the law requiring disclosure of who paid for political communications to internet political communications. Should this proposal be adopted?
plainEnglish: This asks voters to adopt a state law about campaign contributions and political messages.

Regulated electric and gas utilities could not give campaign money to people running for, or holding, offices that affect those utilities. The same ban would cover contractors who receive more than $250,000 a year in government contracts, and people or organizations with substantial ties to those utilities or contractors. Both direct and indirect contributions would be banned.

Rules that already cover campaign spending and donor disclosure would also cover messages that clearly name a candidate or a ballot question, even when the message does not explicitly say to vote for or against them.
Those disclosure rules would expressly cover political messages on the internet, including a requirement to say who paid for them.
A yes vote adopts this law. A no vote leaves current law as it is.
summary: This initiated law would prohibit regulated electric and gas utilities, government contractors with more than $250,000 a year in government contracts, and people or organizations with substantial connections to them from making direct or indirect campaign contributions to candidates for offices that affect them. It would also extend donor-disclosure rules to more political communications, including communications that identify a candidate or ballot question without expressly advocating a vote, and to internet political communications. A yes vote adopts the law. The county list spells “utilities” as “Utilites”; that spelling is left as printed.

title: Corrections and detention millage
officialText: Shall Kent County levy 0.98 mill ($0.98 per $1,000 of taxable value) on the taxable value of all real and personal property subject to taxation for the period 2026 through 2045 inclusive to expand, remodel, equip, operate, maintain, and defray debt service for Kent County Correction and Detention Facilities? This millage is a renewal of the previously authorized millage which expires following the 2029 levy as well as an authorization to increase the existing millage by 0.2468 mill ($0.2468 per $1,000 of taxable value). The amount raised by the proposed levy in the first calendar year is estimated at $37,326,699.00. To the extent permitted by law, a portion of the revenues from this millage will be captured by local authorities for authorized purposes. The total amount of captured tax increment revenues from such millage in the first calendar year of the levy is estimated at $1,497,204.07. The authorities in Kent County capturing a portion of the revenues from this levy include the following: the Downtown Development Authorities for the Cities of Cedar Springs, Grandville, Lowell, Rockford, Walker, the Charter Township of Cascade, and the Townships of Bowne, Sparta, and Tyrone; the Brownfield Redevelopment Authorities of Grand Rapids, Grandville, Kentwood, Rockford, Walker, and Wyoming; and the Monroe North Tax increment Financing Authority of the City of Grand Rapids, Local Development Financing Authority of the City of Grand Rapids, and the Corridor Improvement Authority of the City of Grand Rapids.
plainEnglish: This asks Kent County voters to approve a property tax for the county’s correction and detention facilities, including the jail.

The tax would be 0.98 mill, which is $0.98 for every $1,000 of taxable value, each year from 2026 through 2045. The money would pay to expand, remodel, equip, operate, and maintain those facilities, and to pay debt for them.

This both renews and increases an existing tax. The current millage would otherwise end after the 2029 levy. This proposal renews it and raises it by 0.2468 mill, which is an extra $0.2468 per $1,000 of taxable value.

Kent County estimates the tax would raise $37,326,699 in the first year. Of that, about $1,497,204 is expected to be kept by local development authorities — such as downtown, brownfield, and corridor authorities in listed cities and townships — for their own authorized projects. The official wording names those authorities.
summary: Kent County asks voters to levy 0.98 mill, which is $0.98 per $1,000 of taxable value, from 2026 through 2045 for correction and detention facilities. The county’s 2026 certified rate is 0.7332 mill and continues through the 2029 levy if this fails. The ballot increase is 0.2468 mill. The dollar lines above follow the taxable value entered on this page. The county estimates $37,326,699 in the first calendar year, and about $1,497,204.07 captured by the tax-increment authorities named in the ballot wording.

title: Zoo and museum millage
officialText: For the purpose of renewing dedicated funding for the care of animals and artifacts, repair and improvement of exhibits, and providing enhanced educational programs, shall the total limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all taxable property in Kent County be renewed at 0.4086 mill ($0.4086 on each $1,000 of taxable value) on all Real and Personal Property subject to taxation for the period 2026 through 2035, inclusive, which would be allocated to the John Ball Zoo and the Grand Rapids Public Museum? The amount raised by the levy in the first year is estimated at $15,562,948.00. To the extent permitted by law, a portion of the revenues from this millage will be captured by local authorities for authorized purposes. The total amount of captured tax increment revenues from such millage in the first calendar year of the levy is estimated at $399,110.86. The tax increment authorities in Kent County, capturing a portion of this tax levy, include the following: the Downtown Development Authorities for the Cities of Cedar Springs, Grandville, Lowell, Rockford, and Walker, the Charter Township of Cascade, the Townships of Bowne, Sparta, and Tyrone; the Brownfield Redevelopment Authorities of Cascade Township, Cedar Springs, Grand Rapids, Grandville, Kent County, Kentwood, Plainfield Charter Township, Rockford, Walker, and Wyoming; the Monroe North Tax increment Financing Authority; and Corridor Improvement Authority of the City of Grand Rapids.
plainEnglish: This asks Kent County voters to renew a property tax for John Ball Zoo and the Grand Rapids Public Museum.
The rate would stay 0.4086 mill, which is $0.4086 for every $1,000 of taxable value, each year from 2026 through 2035.
The money is dedicated to caring for animals and museum artifacts, repairing and improving exhibits, and offering more educational programs.

Kent County estimates the tax would raise $15,562,948 in the first year. Of that, about $399,111 is expected to be kept by local development authorities — such as downtown, brownfield, and corridor authorities in listed cities and townships — for their own authorized projects. The official wording names those authorities.
summary: Kent County asks voters to renew 0.4086 mill, which is $0.4086 per $1,000 of taxable value, from 2026 through 2035 for the John Ball Zoo and the Grand Rapids Public Museum. The 2025 rate was 0.4134 mill. MLive reported on May 12, 2026 that the current millage expires at the end of 2026. The dollar lines above follow the taxable value entered on this page. The county estimates $15,562,948 in the first year, and about $399,110.86 captured by the tax-increment authorities named in the ballot wording.
